zh.prompt: 数据显示：每天刷手机超 3 小时的学生，成绩平均低一个档次。但同一份报告附注，这批学生里家庭监督较弱的比例也更高，且「低一个档次」仅来自三所城市的抽样。据此，关于「刷手机与成绩」能得出多强的结论？
hints: 相关不等于因果——也许成绩差的学生才更爱刷手机
「低一个档次」背后是多少人、什么学校？样本仅三城
结论要匹配证据强度，别滑向任何一端
zh.explanation: 这份数据只支持「刷手机时长与成绩存在相关性」。因果方向可能相反（成绩差才更爱刷），也可能有第三因素（家庭监督）同时影响两者；且样本仅三城，推广存疑。合理结论落中段偏左：有关联，但不能断言因果，更别滑向「毁掉」或「无关」。

en.prompt: Data shows students on phones over 3 hours daily score one grade lower on average. But the same report notes these students were also more likely to come from weakly-supervised homes, and 'one grade lower' comes only from samples in three cities. Based on this, how strong a conclusion about 'phone use and grades' is reasonable?
hints: Correlation is not causation — maybe lower achievers use phones more
How many students, which schools, sit behind 'one grade lower'? Only three cities
The conclusion must match the evidence's strength; don't slide to either end
en.explanation: This data only supports 'phone time and grades are correlated'. The causal direction could be reversed (weaker students use phones more), or a third factor (parental supervision) could affect both; the three-city sample also limits generalization. The reasonable conclusion sits left of center: there is a link, but causation cannot be asserted, let alone 'ruins' or 'unrelated'.
